batch_metadata.source: user-collected screenshots/PDFs, mixed origin (Reddit and other)
batch_metadata.confidence_note: Only record 9 (Chino Heating and Cooling) has a named contractor and dated quote. All others are anonymous screenshots with no confirmed location or date — treat as directional/pattern evidence, not location-grounded pricing comps. Do not use these to answer a user's 'is my quote fair for my area' question without a location match.

records.notes: Same bundle structure as batch2026-08-03. Notably the 'Best' tier here is CHEAPER than 'Better' ($17,650 vs $17,803) despite being labeled higher - the brand (Carrier vs Rheem) is the differentiator, not spec superiority, since SEER2/AFUE are nearly identical. Good example of tier-label != strict price/quality ordering, worth flagging to users who assume 'Best' always costs the most.

diagnosis.complaint: AC not keeping up with outdoor temps, home progressively warming over several days, system unable to reach thermostat setpoint
findings: Evaporator coil (replaced 2021) in good condition, no rust/corrosion
Evaporator cabinet sweating excessively - indicates system not operating under normal conditions
Blower motor and air filter operating properly, no concerns
No evidence of coil freeze-over during inspection
Condenser coil cleaned prior to testing
Refrigerant pressure readings indicate restriction within the line set, causing excess compressor strain, risk of premature compressor failure if uncorrected

scope: Nitrogen flush and cleanout of line set to remove contamination/restriction

records.confidence: low - no location/date/contractor, but diagnostic narrative is detailed and internally consistent
records.notes: Strong repair-path example with a clear diagnostic chain (symptom -> inspection -> finding -> root cause -> fix). Useful reference for what a well-documented repair estimate should look like, and for repair-vs-replace cost anchoring ($3,471 repair vs $8,000-11,000+ replacement quotes elsewhere in this batch).

soft_guarantees: Peace of Mind Guarantee - background-checked and randomly drug-tested technicians
Property Protection Guarantee - protects shrubs, lawns, carpeting, floors, walls, furniture, door frames; shoe covers and hall runners used; liability and workmen's comp insurance carried
records.notes: Lowest sticker price in the batch for a full replacement, but single-stage/standard-efficiency equipment throughout. Heavy emphasis on trust/guarantee marketing language rather than equipment specs - useful example of how contractors sell on service assurances when equipment tier is basic.

equipment.condenser: Ruud 3 ton 13.8 SEER2 AC, model RA14AY36AJ1NA, R-454A

scope: Remove existing furnace and coil in attic and condenser at exterior
Install new furnace/coil/condenser in place, reconnect to existing ductwork, gas, electric, condensate, lineset, and flue pipe with new return air plenum
Enlarge return air (existing not sized for R454A CFM requirements - system will ice over if not addressed)
Install extension and new electrical disconnect, mounted next to condenser to meet local code
Re-hang system using Unistrut and all-thread to meet local code (currently hung with metal drives, out of code)
Existing thermostat to remain and be reused
terms: Permits paid by owner as extra
Equipment models may vary, subject to availability
Payment schedule: 50% due on acceptance, 50% due on completion
records.confidence: high - only record in batch with named contractor and confirmed quote date
records.notes: Most traceable/usable record in this batch for future location-grounding if the property location can be confirmed. Flags an important technical detail worth teaching Mike to watch for: undersized return air relative to new refrigerant type CFM requirements causing coil icing - this is a legitimate scope item, not upselling, and a good example of a contractor explaining WHY extra work is needed rather than just listing it.
